look: Dark planetarium with a translucent pill-shaped heading strip, Skyrim style.
borrow: Copy js/ui/gyro.js as the sensor layer: iOS permission, both orientation events, screen rotation, shortest-path smoothing.

look: A map that turns to match the way you face, with a small compass button.
borrow: The circular-mean smoother (about 15 lines). Use 10–20 samples, not 100, or it lags.

look: A full open-source maps app; the compass is a small control that rotates smoothly.
borrow: spring.ts: a critically damped angular spring that settles without overshoot. Lower the damping for a retro wobble.

look: Location-based AR toolkit: 3D objects placed at real coordinates around the camera.
borrow: The maintained replacement for three.js DeviceOrientationControls, if the compass becomes a 3D object.

look: A plain round dial with a permission button and a heading readout.
borrow: The smallest correct end-to-end example (about 360 lines). A good starting template.

look: No UI. A tilt-compensated heading formula from the W3C spec.
borrow: Use the formula if people will hold the phone upright.

look: No UI. Historical; no iOS permission support.
borrow: The idea of calibrating the heading against GPS course while walking, as an indoor fallback.

look: Off-the-shelf brass, metal or gold instrument bezels with glass highlights and a knob.
borrow: new steelseries.Compass(canvas, {frameDesign: BRASS}): a brass compass in one line, with an elastic needle.

look: Clean, themeable radial and linear gauges; a radial gauge can be set up as a compass.
borrow: Ready compass config. Set useMinPath: true or the needle spins the long way at north.
quote: “Radial gauges are an example of bad skeuomorphism.” / “They're the quickest way to convey a scalar value at a glance.” (HN)

look: Realistic aircraft cockpit instruments, including a heading indicator.
borrow: The technique: stack SVG layers and rotate only the card. GPL, so redraw rather than copy.

look: A racing-game heading strip with ticks, labels and fading edges.
borrow: The cleanest Skyrim/Forza strip found: about 90 lines, wrap-safe tick maths, ports easily to React or vanilla JS.

look: Green-phosphor fighter-jet HUD with a heading tape, meant for a car windscreen.
borrow: The look only. AGPL licence, and its sensor code has bugs.

look: An antique brass-and-parchment “alethiometer” from His Dark Materials, with emoji around the dial.
borrow: The strongest magic-instrument look found. GSAP Draggable rotation with snapping makes a satisfying manual dial for laptops.

look: Neon-green radar sweep with additive glow over a live map.
borrow: The technique: PixiJS additive blending gives glow without writing shaders. No licence, so don't copy code.

look: A traditional Chinese geomancer's compass: dense gold-on-black rings, plus camera and lock modes.
borrow: The idea of a dense multi-ring dial and a lock button. Don't reuse its images. Broken on iOS 13+ (no permission call).

look: A compass that points at one target instead of north.
borrow: The bearing formula and needle angle = bearing − heading. Avoid its Android bug (raw relative alpha).

look: Minecraft Eye of Ender: an emerald ring with an arrow pointing to a server-chosen spot.
borrow: Proof that one Svelte + Tailwind page is enough. Not wrap-smoothed.

tech: Vue SVG inside a three.js portfolio
look: An Apple-Watch-style dial with red north, cardinals and waypoint dots.
borrow: Clean SVG structure (rotating card, fixed needle, waypoints) and an idle-spin mode when there is no sensor.

look: Fallout Pip-Boy screen in phosphor green with a moving scan line.
borrow: The CRT scan-bar recipe (easy to rewrite). GPL; the repo also contains a hard-coded API key, so copy nothing.

look: A watch face that morphs from a round rose (held flat) to a heading strip (held upright).
borrow: The rose-to-strip morph and a 5-line spring that gives the needle inertia.

look: A simple compass rose you drag to pick a direction.
borrow: Public-domain drag-to-set-bearing pattern, useful on laptops or to aim the physical needle.

look: A faithful clone of the iOS 7 Compass app, with a bubble level.
borrow: Mostly the bugs to avoid: webkitCompassHeading || alpha fails at 0°, and Android is mirrored.

look: A red-and-white 3D needle that tilts with the real magnetic field.
borrow: The 3D dip-needle idea. Needs a Chrome flag, so not demo-ready.

look: Photoreal aged-brass pocket compass with hinged lid and engraved dial.
borrow: Fastest route to a photoreal 3D brass hero object. Check that the needle is a separate mesh first.

look: Ornate procedural compass roses in old-map styles and palettes.
borrow: A procedural rose seeded per user or destination could be the remix angle.
quote: “Man, they are so beautiful.” / “SVG export would be even better.” (itch.io)

look: A card that tilts in 3D as you move the phone.
borrow: Cheap CSS 3D tilt parallax for a skeuomorphic dial. Avoid its CSS transition on raw yaw.

look: A rotating outer dial with needle, N/E/S/W and a heading/lat/long readout.
borrow: Praise went to the look; every complaint was a sensor-axis bug. Test iOS and landscape before the demo.
quote: “a very attractive design, despite it's technical difficulties.” / “The outer ring rotates twice as much as I physically rotate my phone.” (HN)

look: One floating green 3D arrow that always points at the centre of the galaxy.
borrow: A single poetic target drew 175 points, not visual complexity. Use quaternions if the phone is held upright.
quote: “the drawn arrow totally breaks down when the phone is held vertically.” (HN)

look: A 3D ship's cabin chart table at sea, with a compass among nine clickable objects.
borrow: Brass-and-lacquer nautical mood, adaptive quality, and a fallback without WebGL.
quote: “Great vibes, and verrry nice/clean presentation!” (three.js forum)

look: A liquid-damped skeuomorphic compass: the card swings past and settles, with a lit bearing display and knurled bezel.
borrow: Best modern skeuomorphic reference: physical overshoot plus real screen-reader semantics.

look: A minimal dial with accuracy readout, calibration dialog and map view.
borrow: Tune smoothing; people notice both jitter and lag. Show calibration state and a true/magnetic north toggle.
quote: “Pretty snappy, almost matches the refresh rate and latency of the iphone's compass app.” (HN)

look: A browser 3D arrow that points to each planet as you turn, with a camera overlay.
borrow: A no-login web sensor compass is well received. Design the desktop/no-sensor screen on purpose.
quote: “Love this idea and love that you've not required registration.” (Product Hunt)

look: A compass that lists landmarks in the direction you point, with sun direction and golden hour.
borrow: The content around the dial carries the product. The maker's next idea is a game-minimap face.
quote: “I love it and the idea is so unique!” (Product Hunt)

look: Pick a photo and an arrow points to where it was taken.
borrow: “Point at a memory” suits Retro Remix. iOS web uploads may strip photo GPS data; test first.
quote: “The compass isn't updating for me in iphone 6.” (HN)

look: Shows the first country you would hit going straight where you point, on maps from 1 BC to 1900 AD.
borrow: Old maps through a compass fits the theme. Show uncertainty as a cone, not a line.
quote: “if I face 270, I get Canada, but if I face 269.9, I get Mexico.” (HN)

look: A curved game-HUD ring of 24 planes with yellow cardinals and quest/enemy icons.
borrow: A Skyrim/Fallout strip as a second view alongside the round dial, in plain CSS.

look: A three.js night sky with a star to find and a 2D arrow guiding you to it.
borrow: Ask for sensor permission in an onboarding step; cheap 3D-target to 2D-arrow maths.

look: Real boat-tablet instruments: compass card, waypoint bearing, wind gauge.
borrow: Sailors want a ship's-compass card and high contrast. Contrast beats ornament in daylight.
quote: “I find the compass dials a win- but they are hard to read.” (OpenMarine forum)

look: A Fallout Pip-Boy-themed compass and map in glowing green.
borrow: Pip-Boy green is a proven nostalgic skin. Users asked for destinations on the dial.
quote: “I just wish you could plot destinations on it and then it would be truly perfect.” (App Store)

look: A see-through compass face with a floating ring, damped by eddy currents.
borrow: Transparent-face motif for a glass UI. A needle-settling demo must look honest; HN spotted edits.
quote: “By removing the plate and adding the ring, you can see through the face” (HN)

look: A 3D marine compass card rendered in the browser.
borrow: Historical: a 3D web marine card is an old idea, so novelty must come from elsewhere.

look: An animated compass driven by one number input.
borrow: Could be driven by the heading through a Rive state machine.

look: A charting-library compass gauge.
borrow: A quick gauge if the team already uses amCharts.

look: A game of solar orientation: find directions from the sun.
borrow: Real navigation knowledge as the interaction.

look: A geography game where you aim a compass at cities on a globe.
borrow: Aim-the-compass as a game mechanic.

look: An astrolabe-inspired watch face.
borrow: Astrolabe styling as an alternative to a plain rose.

look: A professional ship-bridge design system with instrument components.
borrow: Real maritime UI conventions. Not confirmed to include a compass.
